subject: Request: custom SLA addendum & order form language for MedAlign enterprise onboarding
messages:
From: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@medalign.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Aug 2025 09:24:00 -0700
Subject: Requesting a custom SLA addendum for MedAlign enterprise MSA

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement at MedAlign has reviewed the standard MSA/SOW and we need to confirm whether Redwood can deliver a custom SLA addendum for our enterprise onboarding. High-level asks from our side: 

- Availability: target 99.95% monthly for production traffic across two regions (primary + failover).
- Latency: p95 inference latency <= 300ms for our standard 2k token payloads under steady-state load (we can provide traffic profile).
- Evidence & auditability: SOC2 reports, 90-day incident history summary, per-route latency percentiles, and orderable telemetry hooks for key endpoints.
- Order form language: an explicit availability exhibit or exhibit + order form rev that ties credits to per-region availability.

Can you: (1) confirm whether you can provide those commitments as an addendum to the MSA/SOW, (2) share a timeline for draft language + internal approvals, and (3) send any evidence packages you can share with procurement/legal?

Attached: MedAlign_RFP_SLA_req.pdf (our internal asks). Ideally we would have draft language and DocuSign-ready order form within two weeks to keep our onboarding timetable.

Best,
Sarah Lim
Senior Procurement Manager
MedAlign Health
procurement@medalign.com

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear ask and the attachment. We can support a tailored availability exhibit and a corresponding order form amendment; below is a practical path-forward and the pieces we'll need from MedAlign to finalize language.

What Redwood can offer (options):
- Dedicated capacity pool (reserved GPUs) + regional failover configuration — aligns with 99.95% target when configured with cross-region fallback.
- Availability exhibit to sit behind the MSA that includes: uptime metric, measurement method, service credit schedule, and force-majeure carveouts.
- Latency commitment as an operational target (p95) combined with telemetry hooks and a runbook for incident classification.

What we need from you:
- Confirmation of accepted measurement window (monthly) and whether credits should be applied per-region or globally.
- A traffic profile (token-per-minute distribution) and the 2–3 representative endpoints you want prioritized.

Internal next steps / timeline: 
- Today: I’ll route this to legal and procurement (cc'd Marissa) and to infra (cc'd Karthik) for feasibility and evidence pull.
- 48–72 hours: draft availability exhibit + candidate order form language (wording for the order form annex).
- 5–10 business days: finalized language post-legal review and a DocuSign-ready order form.

Attachments I’m sending now: redwood-uptime-evidence-pack.pdf (contains recent rolling-90d availability + incident summaries), and an internal example orderform-draft.docx for you to review.

If MedAlign is comfortable, can we schedule a 30-minute call tomorrow to align measurement details? Proposed slots: 10:00–10:30 PT or 14:00–14:30 PT.

Thanks — Evelyn

Subject: Re: Requesting a custom SLA addendum for MedAlign enterprise MSA

Evelyn / Karthik — quick legal/procurement signal so we can move faster with MedAlign: 

Summary of proposed order form language (starter text):
"Availability Exhibit: Provider will maintain Customer-facing availability of 99.95% per calendar month for Covered Services. Availability will be measured as total uptime for the production endpoint(s) listed in the Order Form, excluding scheduled maintenance and force majeure events. Service credits shall be calculated as a percentage of monthly recurring fees according to the schedule in Appendix A."

Operational clarifications we should include (suggested bullets for Exhibit):
- Measurement methodology: median of per-minute health-checks across the primary region; cross-region failover windows excluded only if routed via Redwood's automated fallback.
- Latency: include p95 operational target with transparency clause — failure to meet p95 triggers an operational remediation plan rather than monetary credits (company policy prefers credits only to availability breaches).
- Evidence & audit: we will provide SOC2 attestation and a rolling 90-day incident summary; for deeper telemetry we propose a time-limited access token for read-only metrics export to MedAlign's security team.

Procurement ask: we need to confirm whether MedAlign expects credits for latency misses. If yes, run this through pricing to surface an uplift.

Karthik — can infra provide a short note (1 pager) on how fallback windows are measured and any known historical variance? I can fold that into the evidence pack for procurement.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Contracts & Legal Operations, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
